source.title: Dataset Distillation for Pre-Trained Self-Supervised Vision Models
source.authors: George Cazenavette; Antonio Torralba; Vincent Sitzmann

record.file_problem: none; full paper and appendix are present.
record.tranche_reason: Measures pairwise model alignment with mutual k-nearest-neighbor alignment, the measure attributed to the Platonic Representation Hypothesis, on the paper's pretrained vision models. It does not test alignment changing with scale.
record.gate_note: Table 6 directly reports pairwise embedding-space alignment and is recorded below. The normalized k-NN accuracy values in the same table are cross-model performance of distilled datasets, not direct representation-alignment measurements, so they are not rows. Other dataset-distillation results and cited findings do not directly test the claim.
record.test_reason: Section 4.6 / Table 6 reports PRH mutual k-NN alignment for six pairs of four ViT-B vision models with different objectives (CLIP, DINO-v2, EVA-02, MoCo-v3) on ImageNet-1k. This is a single snapshot, so it bears only on V7's claim that alignment is far from complete. The measurement is a side result: it serves as ground truth for the paper's distillation method. There is no scale sweep, no seed comparison and no metric comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The paper is mainly a dataset-distillation method for linear probes on pre-trained backbones. As a side interpretability result, it notes the models are 'not yet perfectly synchronized' and that distilled-data cross-model performance correlates with mutual k-NN alignment (no coefficient given). It also argues that distilled images visualize model misalignment, e.g. CLIP vs MoCo.
record.recipe_differences: Uses mutual k-nearest-neighbor alignment as described in the cited Platonic Representation Hypothesis work, but the paper does not state the k setting for the alignment matrix. This is an empirical paper, not a replication package.

fits_no_version.finding: Datasets distilled with one backbone train linear probes on other backbones fairly well: normalized 1-NN accuracy is 46.6–95.5 (Table 6 left; Table 2). The authors say this tracks mutual k-NN alignment row by row, but they give no correlation coefficient.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-model transfer of model-specific synthetic training data tracks representational alignment between the models.

record.problems: The alignment matrix reports no uncertainty estimates, and the study measures only a small set of model pairs and one stated dataset setting; it has no scale or capability sweep.
record.rows_left_out: The normalized k-NN accuracy entries in Table 6 are cross-model distilled-dataset performance, not direct representation-alignment measurements. The diagonal self-alignment entries (1.00) are cited as the reference in the retained rows rather than recorded as independent-model results.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep. All models are ViT-B.
No mapping or stitching between representations. Cross-model transfer of distilled images is a different construct.
No feature, neuron or circuit comparison.
No variation of the metric, k or inputs.
Plateau, and whether shared data or objectives explain the alignment, are not tested. Only the incompleteness is measured.

missing.what: The k value and number of samples used for the mutual k-NN alignment matrix, and whether the inputs are the ImageNet-1k train or test split. These are needed to compare against PRH numbers.

record.verdict_notes: This is a weak test. The alignment matrix is ground truth for validating the distillation method, not a study of convergence. A single snapshot of four same-size models cannot speak to V1's trend. The 'far from complete' reading depends on mutual k-NN's scale, and PRH itself reports similar magnitudes. The tests/T1 classification is borderline; uses_without_test/T4 would also be defensible.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep; no test of alignment increasing with model size or capability.
No comparison of representations of paired images and captions, or of alignment changing as vision and language models improve.
No same-architecture, different-initialization comparison or analysis of shared features or subspaces across seeds.
Cross-model use of distilled images is not a test of mapping one model's representations onto another's.
No comparison of interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits across models.
No comparison of alternative similarity measures, settings such as k, or input distributions for their effect on measured alignment.
Measures whether the tested models are perfectly aligned, but does not test whether alignment plateaus or whether shared training data or objectives explain it.
